definition: Jollo was an online machine translation service where users could instantly translate texts into 23 languages, request human translations from a community of volunteers around the world, and compare the correctness of several leading machine translation websites.

explainer.lead: Jollo was an online machine translation service offering instant translation into 23 languages, community human translation, and comparison of leading machine translation sites. It shows how early translation tools mixed automated output with volunteer correction.

tiers.eli5: It was a website where you could get text translated by a machine, ask a volunteer to translate it properly, or see how different translation sites did on the same text.
tiers.practitioner: It is a historical reference point for evaluating translation systems side by side; no current engineering use follows from it, and the service was discontinued in 2012.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition or formula is given for Jollo; the known limit is that the service was discontinued in 2012.

explainer.example: A user could submit a text, receive instant machine output in one of 23 languages, and compare it against results from other leading translation websites.
